system_metadata.author: Dan Olsen
system_metadata.grounding_source: The Lean Product Playbook: How to Innovate with Minimum Viable Products and Rapid Customer Feedback (2015)

space_pen_mirage.analogy: Paul Fisher spending $1 million of his own money to invent the Space Pen to write in zero gravity, while Russian astronauts used cheap pencils.
space_pen_mirage.risk: Jumping into the solution space prematurely without defining the core problem statement.
space_pen_mirage.action: Force separation of 'What' (Problem Space) from 'How' (Solution Space) before design begins.

follow_me_home.analogy: Intuit employees waiting at retail stores, buying Quicken with customers, and following them home to watch them install and use the software.
follow_me_home.action: Prioritize direct behavioral observation of actual setup and friction over polite survey comments.

oprah_versus_spock.analogy: Oprah (qualitative, attitudinal, one-on-one deep conversations) versus Spock (quantitative, behavioral, pure numbers and A/B test data).
oprah_versus_spock.action: Use Oprah to define and validate the product-market fit on paper; use Spock to optimize metrics after launch.

silver_bullet_metric.analogy: Friendster's Yahoo Address Book Importer, which doubled the 'Average number of invites sent per sender' from 2.3 to 5.3 in one week of development.
silver_bullet_metric.action: Identify low-effort, high-upside opportunities that yield exponential compound growth.

local_maximum_hill.analogy: Optimizing a landing page to death and hitting a local peak, while missing the global maximum mountain that requires a complete pivot in the business model.
local_maximum_hill.action: If iterative testing yields diminishing returns, zoom out to re-evaluate the target customer or core value proposition.

olsen_hierarchy_of_web_needs.5_ux_design: How easy and enjoyable the product is to use.
olsen_hierarchy_of_web_needs.4_feature_set: The functionality provided to meet a customer need.
olsen_hierarchy_of_web_needs.3_absence_of_bugs: The quality level - does it work as supposed to?
olsen_hierarchy_of_web_needs.2_page_load_time: The performance - response time must be fast enough.
olsen_hierarchy_of_web_needs.1_uptime: The baseline availability of the service when wanted.

must_haves.definition: Table stakes or cost of entry. Their presence does not increase satisfaction, but their absence causes extreme dissatisfaction.
must_haves.example: Seat belts or cup holders in a car.

performance_features.definition: Linear 'more is better' needs. Customer satisfaction increases proportionally as the need is more fully met.
performance_features.example: Fuel efficiency (MPG) or page load speed.

delighters.definition: Unexpected wow factors that provide a pleasant surprise. Their absence does not cause dissatisfaction.
delighters.example: GPS navigation in the 2000s or background photos changing daily.

kano_model_categories.migration_rule: Yesterday's delighters become today's performance features and tomorrow's must-haves.

invest_user_story_rubric.N: Negotiable (not an explicit contract, open to discussion)
invest_user_story_rubric.V: Valuable (delivers clear benefit to the end user)
invest_user_story_rubric.E: Estimable (scope can be reasonably estimated by developers)
invest_user_story_rubric.S: Small (short scope, large epics must be broken down)
invest_user_story_rubric.T: Testable (has clear acceptance criteria to confirm completion)

ux_iceberg_layers.visual_design: Top - typography, colors, iconography, and style guides.
ux_iceberg_layers.interaction_design: Upper Middle - user flows, decision blocks, state models, and flowcharts.
ux_iceberg_layers.information_architecture: Lower Middle - sitemaps, navigation hierarchies, and content labels.
ux_iceberg_layers.conceptual_design: Bottom - core design metaphor (e.g. Quicken's paper checkbook conceptual design).

sean_ellis_pmf.question: How would you feel if you could no longer use [product X]?
